system_overview: A practical state machine replication (SMR) style specification of the MultiPaxos consensus protocol for strongly-consistent replication of a log of commands. Unlike abstract Paxos specifications, this model closely mirrors how a real distributed key-value store would implement MultiPaxos, with explicit server replicas maintaining logs of command instances, clients issuing write and read commands, and a leader election mechanism based on ballot numbers.
actors_and_components: Three types of actors: (1) server replicas that participate in consensus, maintain local logs, and may act as leaders or followers; (2) clients represented implicitly through a sequence of pending write and read commands; and (3) an asynchronous network modeled as a monotonically growing set of sent messages (messages may be delayed, duplicated, or effectively lost but retried). Written in PlusCal with the attached translation.
state_variables: Four global state variables: (1) the set of messages that have been sent on the network, (2) per-replica node state including leader identity, current key value, commit progress, ballot numbers (prepared and maximum known), and a log of instance states (each tracking status, command, and voted ballot/command), (3) a sequence of pending client commands not yet processed, and (4) a sequence of observed client events recording the order of request and acknowledgement events.
initial_state: The network is empty. Every replica starts with no leader, a nil key value, zero commit progress, zero ballot numbers, and all log slots empty. The pending commands sequence contains all write commands followed by all read commands. The observed events sequence is empty.
actions: Seven actions per replica, executed in a nondeterministic loop until termination. (1) Become leader: a non-leader picks a fresh higher ballot, resets its preparation state, and broadcasts a prepare message. (2) Handle prepare: a follower receiving a prepare with a higher ballot updates its known ballot and replies with its voted log entries. (3) Handle prepare replies: a leader waiting for preparation collects a majority of replies, marks its ballot as prepared, and adopts the highest-voted commands for each slot. (4) Take new request: a prepared leader picks the next pending command, assigns it to the first empty slot, broadcasts an accept message, and records the request event. (5) Handle accept: a replica receiving an accept with a valid ballot updates its log slot and replies. (6) Handle accept replies: a leader collecting a majority of accept replies commits the slot, applies the command to its key-value state, records the acknowledgement event, and broadcasts a commit notice. (7) Handle commit notice: a follower receiving a commit notice marks the corresponding slot as committed and applies the command.
liveness_properties: Semi-liveness is checked by requiring no deadlocks until all commands have been processed, requested, and acknowledged. An explicit termination condition requires that all pending commands are consumed and all request/acknowledgement events are observed.
additional_assumptions: Several optimizations reduce the state space without loss of generality: ballot numbers from different proposers are unique, commands are picked in a fixed order, and each command appears at most once in a prepared log. The pending command sequence is fixed (writes before reads) since other orderings are symmetric or less interesting. The specification supports extension with features like node failure injection and leader leases.
